title: RSV vaccine (pregnant women and older adults)
what: A vaccine shot against RSV, a virus that causes severe bronchitis and pneumonia in infants and older adults. In pregnancy the vaccine is given to protect the baby.
why: For women late in pregnancy, to protect the baby, and for older adults, as advised by a doctor.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes; usually one shot
tell_doctor: If you are sick now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
How far along the pregnancy is, as the vaccine is given in certain weeks

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are healthy. You will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: In pregnancy the vaccine is given in a certain week. The doctor will tell you the exact timing.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes so the shoulder is easy to uncover.

steps: A doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, sit at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes the spot aches for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes weakness, headache or body aches
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
You can go back to your usual activities
If pregnant: after the birth, tell the pediatrician you had the vaccine
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a rash all over: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Is the vaccine safe in pregnancy?
faq.a: It is given in pregnancy on doctors' recommendations, in certain weeks. Decide together with your doctor.

faq.q: Do I need it every year?
faq.a: Usually not. Ask your doctor whether a repeat is needed.

reminders.text: RSV vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record and, if pregnant, your pregnancy record.
